messages:
mika: Heads-up — we just started seeing a spike in NVIDIA Xid 13 on a subset of GPUs in us-west-2. 45 events across 12 nodes in the last 60m, mostly during large batched inference from inference-serving (namespace: nn-infer).

sam-oncall: Oof. Are these the new rtx6000-type instances? Node list? Can we cordon/drain the worst ones? :eyes:

mika: Yes, rtx6000-48gb. Suspect nodes: gpu-usw2-az1-004, gpu-usw2-az1-009, gpu-usw2-az2-002. Pattern: Xid 13 happens shortly after long KV-cache warmups and > 2k token sequences (models: odin-v1, odin-v1-quant).

priya: I can try to repro on dev. What exact workload config? batch=64? seq=4096?

mika: Repro config from logs: batch_size=64, seq_len ~= 4096, continuous streaming generator with prefix caching enabled. Also saw Xid 31 on a couple of nodes earlier today (maybe unrelated).

mika: dmesg excerpt from gpu-usw2-az1-004:

```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (13:41) at 0x7ff... 
[ 12345.679002] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.680123] nvidia: GPU reported Xid 13, GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

sam-oncall: Ok let's cordon these three now and migrate active pods. I'll run `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data gpu-usw2-az1-004` then keep them offline for monitoring.

jason: Two quick asks: 1) collect DCGM ECC and memory utilization around the event, 2) collect kernel dmesg + nvidia-smi -q for the last hour. PromQL we use: `sum(rate(dcgm_ecc_volatile_errors_total[5m])) by (gpu)` — check for sudden ECC increases.

zhou: Adding prom query for Xid count we surfaced: `sum by (node) (increase(node_gpu_driver_xid_total[1h]))` — we'll correlate to pod owner via `kube_pod_info` join. Also check for NET IRQ/PCI errors on the host.

priya: Repro attempt on dev: ran `python stress_gpu.py --model odin-v1 --seq 4096 --batch 64 --stream` and got an Xid 13 locally after ~20 minutes. Sharing minimal repro script in case infra wants to test: `stress_gpu.py` toggles persistent CUDA contexts and high KV reuse.

mika: Good catch. That suggests it's trigged by long KV cache + large batch. Possible causes: firmware bug, driver regression, or flaky DRAM on cards (ECC). We saw a minor uptick of ECC corrected errors on two GPUs earlier (from `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC`).

jason: Action plan suggestion:
- Cordoned nodes drained (sam) — immediate mitigation.
- Reboot and run `nvidia-bug-report.sh` + collect `nvidia-smi -q` (sam/infra).
- Run firmware/driver roll forward on 1 node in canary before mass rollout (mika/jason).
- Open NV support ticket with logs and repro (mika).
- Runtime change: add automatic model fallback to smaller KV config when Xid 13 triggers repeatedly for a node (jason/priya).

deploy-bot: @mika created ticket INFRA-3124 for NVIDIA support case and attached logs.

sam-oncall: Cordoned and drained gpu-usw2-az1-004 and gpu-usw2-az1-009. Rebooting 004 now and collecting `nvidia-bug-report.sh` to /tmp/bug-004.tar.gz.

zhou: I'll correlate the Xid timestamps with pod scheduling: `kubectl get events --all-namespaces --field-selector involvedObject.node=gpu-usw2-az1-004 --since=2h` then join to `kube_pod_labels`. If it's a specific job template we can patch deployment to lower batch.

priya: Meanwhile, for immediate app-level mitigation I can add a quick heuristic: if we observe >=3 Xid 13s from same node within 30m, reduce model batch by 50% for that route and fall back to model-odin-small. I can push the change as a short-lived config toggle.

mika: That sounds good. Also let's plan a maintenance window to run vendor-recommended firmware (after NV support confirms) and crop any suspect cards if ECC corrected counts keep rising.

jason: Cost note — draining + replacing cards will reduce capacity; recommend prioritizing canary reboots and driver upgrade first before replacement. If replacements needed, we'll coordinate with procurement (lead time ~2-3 weeks for specific SKUs in us-west).

mika: Ok owners: sam = immediate cordon+bugreport+reboot; priy a = runtime fallback config + repro share; jason + mika = NV support + driver/firmware canary; zhou = prometheus correlation dashboard updates and runbook addendum.

sam-oncall: Done for 004/009. 002 still online but under watch. Will post bug report link when uploaded.

mika: Thanks — keep updates here. If anyone else sees Xid 48/79 pop up, please @mention and include pod ids.

(practical notes: Xid 13 correlates strongly to long KV cache usage and large batch sizes in our case; Xid 31/48/79 may be different root causes — here's a short mapping we discussed: Xid 13 = GPU memory / driver hw-reset often triggered by heavy persistent contexts; Xid 31 = GPU page fault / MMU; Xid 48 = GPU error during kernel launch; Xid 79 = thermal / PCI comms. Will validate with NV support.)
